requirement: Accept the exact frozen source fixture without silently changing its semantics.
why_it_matters: Separates a real source-language path from a hand-authored target artifact.

requirement: Reach the compiler's declared checked one-step-at-a-time/IR seam; an ad-hoc source recognizer must be reported separately.
why_it_matters: This is the boundary that shows the backend is actually connected to the compiler rather than to one source string.
applicability: all compiler routes that expose an intermediate handoff

requirement: Record the target-facing operations produced for the fixture.
why_it_matters: Makes the semantic lowering visible before target-specific instruction choices.

requirement: Emit the actual target instruction or target-language stream and retain an inspectable representation.
why_it_matters: Proves the backend reached its real target vocabulary.

requirement: Produce the loadable artifact the target actually consumes and record how it was produced.
why_it_matters: Exposes assembler, linker, object-format, driver, VM, or packaging dependencies instead of hiding them.

requirement: Record every external runtime or execution dependency required by the produced artifact.
why_it_matters: A tiny executable plus a large runtime is different from a standalone executable even when stdout is identical.

requirement: Retain byte-level disassembly or the closest target-appropriate generated-code listing.
why_it_matters: Lets instruction/code-generation changes be reviewed directly.
applicability: all routes where target code is inspectable

requirement: Run on the declared target and observe exactly stdout X with exit status 0, or the target-equivalent oracle.
why_it_matters: A compiler route is not accepted merely because it produced a plausible artifact.
applicability: all executable routes; target-equivalent oracle for non-process targets

requirement: Inputs outside the implemented source subset fail explicitly rather than being silently miscompiled.
why_it_matters: A tiny backend is safer when its boundary is exact.
applicability: routes that intentionally implement only a subset

requirement: After PX-08 passes, record artifact bytes, external dependency bytes, instruction/code size, compile time if relevant, and raw timing only when the timing boundary is declared.
why_it_matters: Turns future backend growth into comparable observations without confusing correctness with speed.
applicability: all routes; timing ratios require a symmetric harness
